messages:
miriam: quick sync — i'm drafting a compact quantization triage + calibration heuristics checklist for the new 70B gguf bring-up. posting proposed steps so we can ship a repeatable intake flow. pls react or add.

raj: thanks — high level or want the full checklist now?

miriam: full-ish. tried to keep each item actionable. main goals: maintain quality (instr-follow + generation fidelity) while saving memory/cost.

conor: what are we treating as the golden metrics? ppl get hung up on ppx only.

miriam: good call. propose multilayered metrics:
- calib ppx delta on heldout LM set (token-level)
- generation divergence (n-gram overlap + edit distance on canonical prompts)
- embedding cos-sim on semantic tasks (>=0.995 target)
- runtime p95 and GPU mem usage
- failure/degeneration rate on safety prompt set

sasha: how big for the calibration set? and do we use deterministic prompts?

miriam: heuristic: golden set = ~200 curated prompts across instr types (summarize, code, math, multi-turn). plus 2k random real-prod examples for activation coverage. calibration batches: 128-256 for numeric stability.

linus: for per-layer sensitivity, prefer KL or MSE?

miriam: use both: KL for softmax/head-sensitive layers, MSE for activations. then make a heatmap and rank layers by relative error. drop-int8 only on layers below threshold.

conor: thresholds? numbers please :)

miriam: rough thresholds (can tweak):
- avg ppx increase < 1.0% => int8 ok
- avg embedding cos-sim >= 0.995 => int8 ok
- gen-token divergence < 0.5% (token-level) => int8 ok
- if any of above fail but ppx delta < 3% consider fp8 hybrid on top-K layers
- if top-3 layers show >5x relative error, mark for fp16 fallback

raj: how do we define "gen-token divergence"?

miriam: run fixed-seed greedy decode on golden prompt set for fp16 vs quantized; measure fraction of tokens that differ at each position and average across examples. also compute BLEU/ROUGE as secondary.

sasha: can we auto-generate the config for a candidate model?

miriam: yes, propose this script snippet for a standard run:
```
# calibration run (example)
python tools/quantize.py \
  --model ./models/70B_fp16.safetensors \
  --out ./out/70B.gguf \
  --bits 8 \
  --method qmap \
  --calib-set ./calib/golden.jsonl \
  --calib-batches 128 \
  --eval-prompts ./calib/golden_prompts.jsonl \
  --seed 42
```
Add `--hybrid-layers "0,1,2"` if you want fp8 only on the top layers.

calib-bot: automated note: calibration job queued (job id 2026). will post per-layer errs + summary when complete.

linus: what's the desired rollout plan? canary + metrics to watch?

miriam: rollout checklist (short):
1) pass calibration thresholds locally
2) run 1k-sample production shadow (no routing) for 24h
3) canary 5% traffic on dedicated pool with fallback to fp16 if token-divergence > 1% or latency p95 regresses by >10%
4) 24h canary, monitor: ppx, gen-divergence, embedding drift, safety triggers, p95 latency, OOMs
5) expand to 25% -> 100% with rolling quotas

conor: cost heuristics? when is int8 actually worth it?

miriam: quick rule: if int8 reduces memory by >=30% and p95 latency roughly equal, it's a win; otherwise weigh cost per-token reduction vs detection risk. estimate: 30% memory -> ~40% instance cost reduction on some GPU families when you can bin-pack more replicas.

raj: any guidance for gguf packaging differences? qc steps?

miriam: yes: include model provenance (commit sha), quant args, calib-set hash, eval summary JSON, and per-layer heatmap as artifacts inside the release dir. example manifest keys: `model:`, `quant_bits:`, `calib_batches:`, `golden_checksum:`.

calib-bot: artifact uploaded: /artifacts/70B/2026-calib-summary.json (summary + per-layer csv).

sasha: who owns followups to make this a template?

miriam: i'll own the initial template. action items:
- miriam: land quant-checklist md in repo + example script (EOD)
- sasha: add golden prompt set draft (50->200) by tomorrow
- raj: wire the post-calib smoke job to our CI (small infra change)
- conor: add cost-estimator snippet to rollout doc
- linus: review layer-threshold heuristics and run 1 pilot on 70B (this week)

conor: :thumbsup: looks good. if pilot runs clean we'll use this as standard intake for new GGUF models.

miriam: thanks all — will iterate. react with :white_check_mark: when you accept your task.
